max_lines.note: Netflix English (USA) rule; no standard binds every platform

max_chars_per_line.note: Netflix English (USA) rule; no standard binds every platform

min_duration.note: Netflix: minimum 5/6 of a second per subtitle event (20 frames at 24 fps). Sources disagree: the BBC subtitle guidelines (https://www.bbc.co.uk/accessibility/forproducts/guides/subtitles/) set no fixed minimum but about 0.3 s per word

max_duration.note: Netflix: maximum 7 seconds per subtitle event. The BBC subtitle guidelines state no fixed maximum duration

max_chars_per_second.source: a reading-speed ceiling often used for adult viewers, written from memory; not read in a primary source during this work
max_chars_per_second.note: working value; Netflix's English guide allows up to 20 characters per second for adult programmes and 17 for children's, so 17 is the stricter children's figure

pause_split.source: mstack default chosen by the builder: a gap this long between two words always starts a new cue

min_gap.source: mstack default chosen by the builder: the shortest pause left between two cues when a cue is lengthened

burn_frames.source: mstack default chosen by the builder: how many cue midpoints are pulled as pictures after burn-in
